question.text: What percent of Americans will oppose the Iran War on the eve of Election Day 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the opposition percentage shown at the Silver Bulletin's [Do Americans support or oppose the Iran War?](https://www.natesilver.net/p/iran-war-polls-popularity-approval) tracker for November 2, 2026, when accessed by Metaculus on or after November 3, 2026.
question.fine_print:
If no value for the exact date is shown, then the closest value preceding it will be used to resolve the question.

Between the value shown in the chart and the csv file under the chart ("Get the data"), the csv file takes precedence.

Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-23 (page header; analyst note signed "EMD, 10/21/26"): The Silver Bulletin tracker shows **36% support and 55% opposition**. The note says support "has ticked up slightly," from 32% at the start of October, and opposition is "down from 60 percent to 55 percent." It also says the Trump administration seems to be holding off on major action until after the midterms while it tries to bring down gas and diesel prices. [Silver Bulletin](https://www.natesilver.net/p/iran-war-polls-popularity-approval)
- 2026-10-16 (earlier update, quoted in the question background): support was 35%, up from an all-time low of 32%. It also says no poll has shown net-positive support since April. [Silver Bulletin](https://www.natesilver.net/p/iran-war-polls-popularity-approval)
- I could not get to the chart or the CSV ("Get the data"), which the question says takes precedence over the chart. The poll list and chart sit behind a subscription prompt, so I can't confirm the exact daily value in the CSV.
- Method: a weighted average using pollster rating, sample size and recency (recency usually counts most), with house-effect adjustments. One snapshot says it uses "more aggressive settings" than Silver's usual averages, so it reacts quickly to new polls. [Silver Bulletin](https://www.natesilver.net/p/iran-war-polls-popularity-approval?open=false)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The latest published figure is 55% opposition, about 10 days before the target date of November 2. The question's range is 49.95 to 62.05.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-25: A Post-ABC-Ipsos poll finds 22% of 2024 Trump voters disapprove of his job performance. [Raw Story](https://www.rawstory.com/i-fell-for-it-three-times-furious-trump-voters-threaten-to-sink-gop-in-midterms/)
- 2026-10-24: RFI cites Reuters/Ipsos: 60% of potential voters are dissatisfied with Trump's handling of Iran. [RFI](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD/20261024-%E7%89%B9%E6%9C%97%E6%99%AE%E5%A4%96%E4%BA%A4%E6%94%BF%E7%AD%96%E6%88%90%E6%9C%9F%E4%B8%AD%E9%80%89%E4%B8%BE%E5%85%B1%E5%92%8C%E5%85%9A%E5%8C%85%E8%A2%B1)
- 2026-10-22: Qantara reports that Iran and the US are timing their negotiating tactics around the midterms, and a deal before the election is unlikely. [Qantara](https://qantara.de/artikel/iran-usa-krieg-warten-auf-die-midterms)
- 2026-10-22: A UMass Lowell national poll finds 71% say the US is spending too much on the war. [UMass Lowell](https://www.uml.edu/news/press-releases/2026/102226-nat-poll-october.aspx)
- 2026-10-21: Change Research for Common Defense (fieldwork Sept 15-28) finds 49% of active-duty troops, military families and veterans oppose the war and 44% support it. [Responsible Statecraft](https://responsiblestatecraft.org/military-poll-iran-war/)
- 2026-10-14: I&I/TIPP is an outlier: 44% support military action, 42% oppose, 14% unsure. It may be part of why the average dropped. [HotAir](https://hotair.com/headlines/2026/10/14/i-and-itipp-poll-finds-surprising-pockets-of-support-for-military-action-against-iran-n3819912)
- 2026-10-08: Pew (fieldwork Sept 28 to Oct 4): 33% approve of Trump's handling of the military action, down from 37% in March. Republican approval fell from 69% to 63%. Asahi reports this as 65% opposed. [Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2026/10/08/iran-conflict-remains-deeply-unpopular-as-many-americans-expect-it-to-go-on-for-months/)
- Early October: more oil is moving through Hormuz despite Iranian attacks, but US gas prices are still high (per the Silver Bulletin note).

## 4. Base rates and trend
- March to May 2026: individual polls showed roughly 53% to 61% opposed (Quinnipiac 53%, Marist 56%, a May poll with 61% calling the war a "mistake"). [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/5/1/poll-finds-61-percent-of-americans-believe-attacking-iran-was-a-mistake)
- Late May 2026: net support was about -22.8 in the average (secondary source). [Factually](https://factually.co/fact-checks/politics/us-public-sentiment-over-possible-war-with-iran-1724d3)
- 2026-07-24 snapshot (reported in search results): 33% support, about 59% oppose.
- Early October 2026: 32% support, 60% oppose, the low point for support.
- About Oct 21-23, 2026: 36% support, 55% oppose.
- So opposition has mostly stayed between about 55% and 60% since spring. The latest value is at the bottom of that band, after a fall of about 5 points in roughly three weeks. That shows the average can move several points within a 10-day window, probably helped by its aggressive recency weighting and by outlier polls like TIPP. The share of undecided respondents (about 9%) also matters: opposition can drop without support rising by the same amount.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market directly on the Silver Bulletin Iran-war opposition figure.
- Related Kalshi markets: "Iran war and foreign policy" as the issue that matters most to voters at 5% (economy 96%); US-Iran nuclear deal before Nov 1 at 1% and before Dec 1 at 7%; Trump approval in the exit poll above 36% at 52%.
- Polymarket: US formally declares war on Iran by Dec 31 at about 2%.
- Manifold: Pentagon gets $200B for the Iran War before the midterms at 5%.
- I could not see the community forecast on Metaculus question 46190.

## 6. Upcoming events before November 2
- New polls from Pew, Reuters/Ipsos, Quinnipiac, Marist, Fox and others are likely before the election. Each one can move the average noticeably.
- Any escalation or major Iranian attack in Hormuz, or a sudden diplomatic deal, could shift opinion. Reporting suggests both sides are waiting until after the midterms.
- Gas and diesel prices: the administration is trying to lower them before the vote.
- Silver Bulletin update timing: if there is no update for November 2 exactly, the closest earlier value counts. The tracker has been updating about weekly (Oct 16, Oct 21-23).

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 8 days until November 2, and the value should be known around November 3.

(b) The latest value is 55% opposition (36% support), from the Silver Bulletin note dated October 21, 2026, published around October 21-23.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be 55%.

(d) If the current trend continued, opposition fell from about 60% to 55% in roughly three weeks. Extending that would give about 52-53%. The drop may partly reflect an outlier poll (TIPP showed only 42% opposed), so some reversion back toward the 56-59% band is plausible as that poll ages out.

(e) Historical variation: the average has mostly stayed between 55% and 60% since spring. It moved about 5 points in 3 weeks, using fairly aggressive recency settings. A typical 10-day move is about 1-3 points, with occasional larger swings.

(f) Expectations of experts and markets:
- No market tracks this exact number.
- Other measures of the war still look broadly unpopular:
  - Reuters/Ipsos found 60% dissatisfied with Trump's handling of Iran.
  - Pew found 33% approve of his handling.
  - UMass Lowell found 71% say the US is spending too much.
- These measure related but different questions, so they argue only weakly for opposition rebounding into the high 50s.
- Reporting suggests the administration is avoiding major escalation before the midterms.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- **Low outcome:** a ceasefire or diplomatic breakthrough, plus falling gas prices and a few friendly polls, could push opposition down to about 51-52%.
- **High outcome:** a major Iranian attack causing US casualties, a spike in gas prices, or a run of high-quality polls showing 60%+ opposed could push the average back to 59-61%.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 55%.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** Opposition fell from 60% in early October to 55% by about October 21. Carrying that slope forward linearly gives roughly 52 to 53%. However, part of the drop likely came from the I&I/TIPP outlier (42% oppose). As that poll ages out, and as more typical polls arrive (Reuters/Ipsos showing 60% dissatisfied with Trump's handling of Iran, Pew at about 65% opposed), opposition would more likely drift back up. On balance, I expect it to stay flat or rebound slightly.

(f) **Experts and markets:** No market tracks this exact figure. Related markets point to no major diplomatic resolution before the election (nuclear deal before November 1 at 1%), and reporting suggests both sides are waiting until after the midterms. The question creator's range is 50 to 62%.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low outcome:** A surprise ceasefire or framework deal, falling gas prices, or several pro-war-leaning polls (TIPP-type) arriving in the final week. Any of these could push opposition to around 51 to 52%.
